result.topic_en: The page ends a fragment on writing px-1 as a square for a prime p=a^2+b^2 (example p=193), then gives fragment 55: the theorem that 4mnz-m-n is never a square, its derivation from divisors of mxx+yy, proofs of the easy residue cases, and the special forms that remain to be shown.
result.transcription:
220 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Arithmetica.
$px = (aa+bb)(cc+dd) = (ac+bd)^2 + (ad-bc)^2$
at $ad-bc = \pm 1$ per hypothesin, unde $px-1 = (ac+bd)^2$.
Exemplum. Sit $p=193$, erit $a=12$ et $b=7$, porro $c=5$ et $d=3$, unde fit
$x=34$ eritque $px-1=81^2$.
A. m. T. II. p. 167.

55.
Theorema numericum profundissimae indaginis.
Si $m$, $n$ et $z$ denotent numeros integros positivos, tum ista formula
$4mnz-m-n$
nunquam evadere potest quadratum.
Hoc theorema inde est derivatum, quod inter divisores formae $mxx+yy$ occurrat formula $4mz+1$, unde sequitur, formulam $4mz-1$ nunquam esse posse divisorem illius formae $mxx+yy$, vel saltem hujus $m+yy$, unde haec aequatio $(4mz-1)n = m+yy$
semper erit impossibilis. Sit $\sqsupset\!\sqsubset$ signum impossibilitatis eritque $(4mz-1)n-m \sqsupset\!\sqsubset yy$ sive $(4mz-1)n-m \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$.
Verum hoc fundamentum nondum est rigide demonstratum, ideoque demonstratio hujus theorematis plurimum desideratur. Interim tamen evidens est ejus veritas casibus, quibus est $m+n=4i+2$, quia tum fit $4mnz-4i-2$ numerus impariter par, a quadrato abhorrens. Dein etiam casu $m+n=4i+1$, quia tum prodit forma $4mnz-4i-1$, sive forma $4A-1$, quae nunquam esse potest quadratum. Demonstrandi igitur tantum restant duo casus, alter, quo $m+n=4i$, alter vero, quo $m+n=4i+3$, vel $4i-1$. Pro casu priore $m+n=4i$ sumi poterit $m=2i-k$ et $n=2i+k$, unde erit $(2i-k)(2i+k)z-i \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, sive $(4ii-kk)z-i \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$.
Pro altero casu, quo $m+n=4i-1$ sumi poterit
$m=2i-k$ et $n=2i+k-1$, eritque $4(2i-k)(2i+k-1)z-4i+1 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$,
sive hoc modo $((4i-1)^2-(2k-1)^2)z-4i+1 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$.
Hinc innumerae formae speciales derivari possunt, veluti ex priore forma $(4ii-kk)z-i \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, unde casu $i=1$
prodit $4z-1 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, $3z-1 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, qui per se sunt manifesti
casu $i=2$: $16z-2 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, $15z-2 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, $12z-2 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, $7z-2 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$
casu $i=3$: $36z-3 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, $35z-3 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, $32z-3 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, $27z-3 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, $20z-3 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, $11z-3 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$
casu $i=4$: $64z-4 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, $63z-4 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, $60z-4 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, $55z-4 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, $48z-4 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, $39z-4 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$
$28z-4 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$, $15z-4 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$.
Hic autem veritas singularum ostendi potest, at vero ex principiis diversissimis. Eodem modo formulae speciales ex altero casu oriundae
$((4i-1)^2-(2k-1)^2)z-4i+1 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$.
sunt casu $i=1$ casu $i=2$ casu $i=3$
$8z-3 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$ $48z-7 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$ $120z-11 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$
$40z-7 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$ $112z-11 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$
$24z-7 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$ $96z-11 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$
$72z-11 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$
$40z-11 \sqsupset\!\sqsubset \square$
A. m. T. II. p. 211. 212.

methods.what: Two-squares product identity applied to px with ad-bc=±1, giving px-1 as a square
Numerical example of px-1 being a square
methods.quote:
Sit $p=193$, erit $a=12$ et $b=7$, porro $c=5$ et $d=3$, unde fit
$x=34$ eritque $px-1=81^2$.

methods.what: Derivation of the theorem from the claim that no divisor of mxx+yy has the form 4mz-1
methods.quote:
formulam $4mz-1$ nunquam esse posse divisorem illius formae $mxx+yy$, vel saltem hujus $m+yy$, unde haec aequatio $(4mz-1)n = m+yy$
semper erit impossibilis

methods.what: Case m+n ≡ 2 mod 4: the number is ≡ 2 mod 4, hence not a square
methods.quote: quibus est $m+n=4i+2$, quia tum fit $4mnz-4i-2$ numerus impariter par, a quadrato abhorrens

methods.what: Case m+n ≡ 1 mod 4: the number is of form 4A-1, hence not a square
methods.quote: casu $m+n=4i+1$, quia tum prodit forma $4mnz-4i-1$, sive forma $4A-1$, quae nunquam esse potest quadratum

methods.what: Reduction of case m+n=4i via m=2i-k, n=2i+k
Reduction of case m+n=4i-1 via m=2i-k, n=2i+k-1
Listed special non-square forms for small i

items.quote:
Si $m$, $n$ et $z$ denotent numeros integros positivos, tum ista formula
$4mnz-m-n$
nunquam evadere potest quadratum.
items.english: If m, n and z denote positive integers, then the formula 4mnz-m-n can never become a square.

items.quote: Verum hoc fundamentum nondum est rigide demonstratum, ideoque demonstratio hujus theorematis plurimum desideratur.
items.english: But this foundation has not yet been rigorously proved, and therefore a proof of this theorem is greatly wanted.

items.quote: Demonstrandi igitur tantum restant duo casus, alter, quo $m+n=4i$, alter vero, quo $m+n=4i+3$, vel $4i-1$.
items.english: Therefore only two cases remain to be proved: one where m+n=4i, the other where m+n=4i+3, or 4i-1.

items.quote: Hic autem veritas singularum ostendi potest, at vero ex principiis diversissimis.
items.english: The truth of each of these can be shown, but from very different principles.
